speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. I need to assess this newborn presenting with respiratory distress. Could you please provide the gestational age at birth and the mother's obstetric history, particularly regarding any diabetes or infections?

speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, born after the 32nd gestational week. The baby was born via cesarean delivery. The mother had gestational diabetes but was otherwise healthy with no other pregnancy-related diseases.

speaker: Doctor
text: Was the baby born immediately after the cesarean section, or were there any complications like meconium aspiration? I also need to know if the baby required immediate resuscitation or respiratory support at birth.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Respiratory distress. I also have Tachypnea, Subcostal and intercostal retractions, Nasal flaring, Cyanosis. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Urinary tract infection and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: That assessment seems inconsistent with the clinical picture, as a urinary tract infection does not typically present with severe respiratory distress, retractions, and cyanosis in a newborn. Given the history of maternal diabetes and cesarean delivery, transient tachypnea of the newborn or respiratory distress syndrome are far more likely causes. REQUEST TEST: Chest_X-Ray

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Ground-glass appearance, air bronchograms, suggesting Respiratory Distress Syndrome (RDS)

speaker: Doctor
text: The chest X-ray findings of ground-glass appearance and air bronchograms, combined with the history of maternal diabetes and preterm birth, strongly point to surfactant deficiency. DIAGNOSIS READY: Respiratory Distress Syndrome (RDS)
